description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

EarthScope Consortium is hiring a Cloud Software Engineer I to develop, maintain, test, and document cloud-based software and systems. The role supports Portable Programs’ scientific data ingestion, processing, quality control, metadata management, and archival workflows, including modernization toward AWS-based services.
Cloud Software Engineer I developing Portable Program data ingestion, processing, quality control, and archival workflows on AWS

Responsibilities:
• Work with project teams and individually to design, develop, implement, and support cloud-based software systems
• Test and document software components, automating tasks whenever possible
• Work with project teams and individually to improve and debug existing functionality
• Participate in joint analysis and design activities with other staff to define directions, standards, timelines, and identification of key technologies for evolving moderately complex software systems
• Participate in platform maintenance activities and component upgrades
• Leverage cloud-native design principles and vendor-specific managed services in software solutions
• May support commercialization efforts as needed
• Other duties may be assigned as necessary for the successful operation of the business
• Develop, maintain, test, and document software applications and tools supporting Portable Program data ingestion, processing, quality control, and archival workflows
• Support maintenance and development of the PASSOFT software suite and related tools, including data2passcal/data2epic, SOHViewer, lemi2seed, phoenix2seed, and associated processing applications
• Contribute to the design, development, testing, and implementation of next-generation nodal data processing workflows, including the transition from PH5-based processing to future AWS-hosted, cloud-based data ingestion and processing workflows, with an emphasis on automation, efficiency, and long-term maintainability
• Support development, modernization, and integration of Portable Program data management applications and databases, including SDB, eQuip, and related systems
• Assist with the development, testing, and deployment of AWS-based data processing, quality control, and batch data submission workflows
• Investigate and resolve software issues affecting operational data processing, metadata management, and archival delivery
• Collaborate with Data Preparation and Capture staff, software engineers, and other technical teams and external users, including the PI community, to identify operational requirements, troubleshoot issues, and implement sustainable software solutions
• Contribute to automated testing, software packaging, deployment, documentation, and knowledge sharing to improve software maintainability and operational continuity
• Support the integration of emerging Portable Program instrumentation, data types, and associated processing workflows
• Other duties may be assigned as necessary for the successful operation of the business

Requirements:
• EarthScope Consortium Inc. is **not able to sponsor employment visas** for this position
• Applicants must be authorized to work and physically reside within the **50 United States**
• Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Systems or related STEM field at time of hire AND Six (6) months of practical software development experience, either as part of an educational project, internship, or equivalent
• At least two (2) years of practical software development experience
• Ability to develop, test, troubleshoot, and maintain software applications supporting scientific data processing and management workflows, including existing and legacy codebases
• Familiarity with one additional programming language such as Java, Typescript, C++ or an equivalent programming language and ability to write modular, reusable code
• Familiarity with Linux-based development environments, command-line tools, databases, data formats, and file-based processing workflows
• Ability to collaborate with scientific and technical staff, external users, and the Principal Investigator (PI) community to understand requirements, troubleshoot issues, and translate operational needs into software solutions
• Ability to create and maintain clear technical documentation, including software functionality, development activities, and troubleshooting procedures
• Familiarity with a collaborative software repository system such as GitHub or GitLab
• Familiarity with Agile practices (continuous integration, test driven development, pair programming, etc.)
• Capability to work on projects using Python, Java, Typescript, C++ or an equivalent programming language and to write modular, reusable code
• Ability to learn new technologies, programming languages, and design patterns; and the ability to incorporate those concepts into projects
• Understanding of the coding life cycle within git including design, development, testing, peer review, and automated deployment
• Disciplined approach to quality engineering via automated testing (Pyunit, JUnit, etc.)
• Ability to work with version control tools like Git, ability to package software that can be deployed with CI/CD
• Familiarity with software containerization (Docker)
• Ability to develop within cloud computing environments, especially AWS
• Familiarity with service-oriented architecture and RESTful web services development
• Familiarity with database design, both SQL and NoSQL, database services, and scripting database queries
• Familiarity with at least one of the following specializations:
• Understanding service-based design, ability to develop and maintain RESTful web services using tools like FastAPI, Spring, Django
• Ability to write front-end applications using tools like Angular, React, or equivalent and integrate those applications with back-end services
• Ability to write Infrastructure as Code using such tools as AWS CDK or Terraform, and an understanding CI/CD pipeline using GitLab CI, Jenkins, or equivalent
• Knowledge of data streaming and stream processing using tools such as Kafka, Flink, or equivalent
• Applicants *MUST* be authorized to work permanently in the United States

Preferred:
• Experience or familiarity with scientific software development and data processing, particularly in geophysics, geodesy, or related Earth science disciplines
• Experience with software repository processes such as MRs, code reviews, pull requests, and CI/CD pipelines
• Familiarity with scientific data formats and processing tools, such as SEED, HDF5, RINEX, or related technologies
• Experience with Python-based scientific computing, data processing libraries, and software packaging tools such as conda or conda-forge
• Familiarity with AWS-based scientific data workflows, including cloud-based processing, data management, and archival systems
• An understanding of earth sciences, earth science data, and the earth science community
